bioprojects.title: Leishmania panamensis MHOM/COL/81/L13 Genome sequencing and assembly
NHGRI Large Scale Sequencing Program for Organismal Sequencing

assembly_info.comments:
Background:
The Leishmania panamensis strain L13 (WHO strain identifier MHOM/COL/81/L13) was obtained from Dr. Nancy Saravia, CIDEIM, Cali, Colombia. This isolate was obtained from a human mucosal lesion from Colombia (Choco, Tado).

Genomic DNA was prepared by CsCl/Ethidium bromide density gradient centrifugation to minimize the amount of kinetoplast (mitochondrial) DNA, and was provided by Drs. Natalia Akopyants and Stephen Beverley, Washington University School of Medicine.

Total sequence coverage of Illumina instrument reads was 165X (300-500bp inserts 65X, 3Kb PE 99X) using a genome size estimate of 35Mb. The combined sequence reads were assembled using the SOAPdenovo software (BGI). This first draft assembly was referred to as L.panamensis L13_1.3. In the L.panamensis L13_1.3 assembly 9343 scaffold gaps were closed with Illumina read mapping and local assembly. No contaminating contigs were removed to yield version L.panamensis L13_1.3.1. The L.panamensis L13_1.3.1. assembly is made up of a total of 1245 scaffolds with an N50 scaffold length of over 156kb (N50 contig length was 22.5 kb). The assembly spans 31.1Mb.

This work was supported by NIH grant AI29646 to SMB and by NIH-NHGRI grant 5U54HG00307907 to RKW, Director of The Genome Institute at Washington University.

For questions regarding this L.panamensis L13_1.3.1 assembly please contact Dr. Wesley Warren, Washington University School of Medicine (wwarren@genome.wustl.edu). Downloads of the sequence data are available via the TriTrypDB genome browser server. Funding for the sequence characterization of the Leishmania panamensis L13 genome was provided by the National Human Genome Research Institute (NHGRI), National Institutes of Health (NIH).
